This can be seen as an essential component of Islamic values, as Islam encourages individuals to be kind, compassionate, and pleasing to others – especially to family, neighbors, and the wider community. In Islam, joy and satisfaction are seen as essential components of a healthy and balanced spiritual life. The Islamic concept of 'khushu' (aimed at creating a feeling of God-consciousness or reverence), for instance, requires an inner sense of joy and melancholic satisfaction, as one contemplates the greatness and beauty of God. Ultimately, the name Nashwaa embodies an Islamic ideal of striving to please and delight God, as well as others, both in daily life and in spiritual pursuits.
